feature_overview.business_goal: To provide secure, reliable user authentication so visitors can create an account and returning users can access the application quickly, with passwords and sessions handled safely by default.
scope: Implement login functionality including form validation and session management.
Implement signup functionality including form validation and password hashing.
feature_overview.feature_boundary: This Architecture Plan covers only the Login and Signup feature and excludes unrelated features.

functional_requirements.description: User can enter email and password into the login form
System validates the input (both fields required, email format correct)
On valid credentials: user receives a success response, is issued an auth session/token, and is redirected to the home page
On invalid credentials: user receives a generic error message ('Invalid email or password') without revealing which field was wrong
User can click 'Show password' to toggle password visibility
User can click a 'Forgot password?' link
User can click a link to go to the Signup page instead
User can enter name, email, password, and confirm password into the signup form
System validates the input (all fields required, valid email format, password meets minimum strength, password and confirm-password match)
System checks whether the email is already registered
If the email is already taken: user receives a clear error message ('An account with this email already exists') and stays on the form
On success: user's account is created, password is hashed before storage, user receives a success confirmation, is automatically logged in, and is redirected to the home page
User can click a link to go to the Login page instead

After a defined number of consecutive failed login attempts (5), the account should be temporarily locked for a cooldown period (15 minutes) or until the account owner resets their password, whichever comes first.

When a user requests a password reset, the system issues a single-use, time-limited reset token (expiring after 30 minutes) sent to the account's verified email address. The token must be invalidated immediately after first use.
Placing an order (checkout) with a newly registered account requires email verification. The customer must be given a clear, immediate way to resend the verification email without losing their cart.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a new, unused email and a valid password, when the user submits the signup form, then their account is created, their password is hashed before storage, and they are automatically logged in and redirected to the home page. Additionally, if the user's email is not verified, placing an order should be blocked until verification is completed.
acceptance_criteria.original_description: Given a new, unused email and a valid password, when the user submits the signup form, then their account is created, their password is hashed before storage, and they are automatically logged in and redirected to the home page

acceptance_criteria.description: Given an email that's already registered, when the user submits the signup form, then they see a clear 'An account with this email already exists' error and remain on the signup page

Given valid login credentials, when the user submits the login form, then they are logged in within 3 seconds and redirected to the sample home page, with the nav bar showing their logged-in state. Additionally, if there have been 5 consecutive failed login attempts, further login attempts should be rejected for a cooldown period of 15 minutes.
acceptance_criteria.original_description: Given valid login credentials, when the user submits the login form, then they are logged in within 3 seconds and redirected to the sample home page, with the nav bar showing their logged-in state

acceptance_criteria.description: Given invalid login credentials (wrong email or wrong password), when the user submits the login form, then they see a generic 'Invalid email or password' error and remain on the login page
Given a logged-in user, when they click 'Logout', then their session ends and they are redirected to the login page
Given a logged-in user, when they refresh the page, then they remain logged in (session persists)

validation_rules.description: Email must be in a valid format.
Password must meet minimum strength requirements.
Confirm password must match the password field.

non_functional_requirements.description: Login and signup responses should complete within 2 seconds under normal load
The system should handle at least 50 concurrent login attempts per second without significant latency
Passwords must be hashed (never stored or logged in plain text) and never returned in any API response
Auth session/token must persist across a page refresh and expire after a reasonable period of inactivity (e.g. 7 days)
Form validation errors must be shown inline, without a full page reload
Failed login attempts should not reveal whether the email or the password was incorrect (prevents account enumeration)

architecture_approach.architecture_rationale: Use monolithic to keep the Login and Signup feature separated into presentation, business logic, and data responsibilities where applicable.
architecture_approach.frontend_overview: Frontend design should provide the user-facing entry points, inputs, states, and feedback required by the approved SRS.
architecture_approach.backend_overview: Backend design should process feature requests, enforce business rules, validate inputs, and return structured responses.
architecture_approach.data_overview: Data design should support the data requirements defined in the approved SRS.
architecture_approach.integration_overview: Integration design should follow the API expectations and dependencies listed in the approved SRS.
design_tradeoffs: Design is derived directly from the approved SRS to preserve traceability and feature scope.
Design is kept feature-scoped to preserve feature-by-feature SDLC development.
Internal generation or repair details are kept in backend logs and are not exposed in the approval-ready Architecture Plan.

Create app/api/auth/login/route.ts implementing /api/auth/login, validating required request fields before use (400 on missing/malformed) -- it is automatically live the instant the file exists, no separate mount step needed.

Create app/api/auth/logout/route.ts implementing /api/auth/logout, validating required request fields before use (400 on missing/malformed) -- it is automatically live the instant the file exists, no separate mount step needed.
Create lib/api/loginAndSignup.ts with one function per endpoint.
Create app/login-and-signup/page.tsx (a Client Component, `"use client"` as its first line), reusing approved UI/UX components where available instead of re-authoring their markup.
Register a real <Link href="/login-and-signup"> in app/page.tsx at the FEATURE_LINKS markers -- a page with no link to it is not complete.
constraints: The Next.js App Router scaffold already exists and works -- never recreate app/layout.tsx, next.config.mjs, tsconfig.json, or lib/mongodb.ts.
A Route Handler (route.ts) is live the instant it exists -- there is no router to mount it on, unlike an Express app.js.
Register new pages by adding a real <Link href="..."> in app/page.tsx (FEATURE_LINKS markers) -- an unreachable page is not done.
Every Mongoose model file must use the `mongoose.models.X || mongoose.model(...)` guard to avoid OverwriteModelError.

Approved UI/UX output is a visual reference, not code to import -- use read_ui_component_design/read_ui_page_design to see the approved HTML+Tailwind design, then write real TSX that faithfully matches its structure/classes/content.
